findings.title: CVE-2026-33824 | Windows Internet Key Exchange (IKE) Service Extensions Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
findings.summary_md: Microsoft published this advisory on April 14, 2026, rating CVE-2026-33824 Critical at CVSS 3.1 9.8 for a CWE-415 double free allowing an unauthenticated attacker to execute code over the network via specially crafted packets to a machine with IKEv2 enabled. The listed mitigations are blocking inbound UDP 500 and 4500 where IKE is unused, or restricting those ports to known peer addresses. Affected products include Windows Server 2016 (KB5082198) and Windows Server 2019 (KB5082123); a revision 1.1 on August 20, 2026 added clarifying mitigation information.

findings.title: CVE-2026-33824: Remote Code Execution in Windows IKEv2
findings.summary_md: This TrendAI Research write-up by Richard Chen and Lucas Miller, published April 23, 2026, details the double free in ikeext.dll that Microsoft's WARP & MORSE team discovered, caused by shallow-copied blob pointers during IKEv2 Encrypted Fragment reassembly, with code execution possible under the IKEEXT service as SYSTEM. Detection guidance is to monitor UDP 500 and 4500 for an IKE_SA_INIT carrying the Microsoft Security Realm Vendor ID byte sequence 68 6a 8c bd fe 63 4b 40 51 46 fb 2b af 33 e9 e8 followed by a fragmented IKE_AUTH with an SKF payload, noting the four-byte non-ESP marker shifts offsets on port 4500.

findings.title: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 - Day Two Results
findings.summary_md: ZDI's Day Two results post from May 15, 2026 records Orange Tsai (@orange_8361) of DEVCORE Research Team chaining three bugs to achieve remote code execution as SYSTEM on Microsoft Exchange, earning $200,000 and 20 Master of Pwn points. The post also notes DEVCORE led the event with 40.5 points and $405,000 through two days, with day-two totals of $385,750 for 15 unique 0-days.
